Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with known SLE on methotrexate presented via telehealth with 1 day of breathlessness, right-sided pleuritic back pain, subjective fever, and two episodes of hemoptysis; video assessment suggested stability; plan for same-day in-person evaluation for suspected chest infection/pneumonia and possible antibiotics.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath and right-sided back pain worse with deep inspiration (pleuritic).
- Hemoptysis: Coughed up blood on two occasions today.
- Fever: Feels warm; temperature not objectively measured (only with back of hand).
- Palpitations/awareness of heartbeat noted.
- Functional impact: Increased fatigue over the past couple of weeks, with reduced exercise tolerance and daily activities harder than usual.
- Onset/timeline:
  - Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance: “Couple of weeks.”
  - Acute symptoms (breathlessness, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, subjective fever): Today.
- Associated/review of systems (as reported):
  - No smoking.
  - No recent long-haul flights.
  - No history of DVT/PE; no family history of clots.
  - No additional symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
  - Background: On methotrexate.
  - No other diagnoses reported.
  - No complications reported during this consult.

Medications:
- Methotrexate — dose/route/frequency not documented; last taken this morning.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies. No other allergies reported.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Occupation: Office/desk job.
- Living situation: Lives alone in a flat.
- Pets: Cat.
- Travel: No recent long-haul flights reported.
- Alcohol/substance use: Not discussed.

Family History:
- No known family history of blood clots. No other family history discussed.

Physical Examination:
- General: Via video, patient did not appear acutely unstable per clinician.
- Pulse: Patient self-count via radial pulse for ~10–11 seconds extrapolated to ~66–74 bpm; rhythm not documented.
- Capillary refill: Video maneuver performed; no abnormality reported.
- Oropharynx: Visualized via phone camera; no abnormalities reported.
- Neck: Patient self-palpation of cervical lymph nodes; no enlargement reported.
- Vitals (BP, temperature, SpO2, respiratory rate): Not measured in this consult.

Investigations:
- None performed during this telehealth visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute respiratory symptoms with hemoptysis and pleuritic pain — suspected chest infection/pneumonia.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange same-day face-to-face assessment in clinic.
    - Perform chest examination with stethoscope; check blood pressure, pulse, and temperature.
    - Consider antibiotics based on in-person findings.
    - Further investigation (e.g., chest X-ray) may be needed depending on examination and clinical course.
    - Support team contact provided for patient to book same-day appointment.
    - No prescriptions issued at this time pending in-person assessment.
- Issue 2: SLE on methotrexate.
  - Plan:
    - Document current immunomodulatory therapy in evaluation and consider in management decisions during in-person review.
- Issue 3: Cancer anxiety (concern about lung cancer due to hemoptysis).
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance provided: Presentation more consistent with acute chest infection; lung cancer typically presents more insidiously.
    - Consider follow-up chest X-ray if symptoms do not settle or as indicated by in-person exam.

General Plan items:
- Patient to call support team to arrange same-day face-to-face appointment with GP.
- Safety netting: Not explicitly documented beyond same-day in-person review.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Full vital signs (BP, temperature, respiratory rate, SpO2).
  - Formal chest auscultation and complete physical exam.
  - Complete medication list with doses/routes/frequencies.
  - Comprehensive systems review (e.g., chest pain beyond pleuritic pain, wheeze, sputum characteristics, leg swelling), travel/TB exposure history.
  - Past medical/surgical history beyond SLE, immunization status.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient name recorded as “Tracy Chapman” at start; later confirmed as “Doris” — conflict noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Several unclear/inaudible segments; some responses truncated. Clinical details may be incomplete due to audio/transcription gaps.
